assessment.nobel_worthiness: Founded modern political economics by formalizing how electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity shape fiscal policy and public-goods provision. The framework is general, theoretically disciplined and empirically productive, and it has shaped work across public economics, development and comparative politics.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini developed the constitutional and electoral-rules program and its book-length synthesis. Besley's contributions on state capacity, political agency and accountability are comparably foundational. The trio is a natural and coherent set. Others, such as Acemoglu on institutions, overlap in theme but not in core contribution.
assessment.maturity: Core work dates from the 1990s and 2000s and has been extensively replicated, extended and taught. Its influence is fully established and the field has had decades to test it.
uncertainties: Thematic overlap with the 2024 institutions prize could reduce its perceived distinctiveness.
Some cross-country constitutional-effects estimates face identification critiques.
I am uncertain whether the committee would want a third person or a different combination.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1997 credit-cycles model showed how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks. It is a workhorse for macro-finance, financial-crisis analysis and policy design, and it connects asset prices, borrowing limits and real activity.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clear originators of the collateral-constraint dynamic amplification mechanism. Gertler and Gilchrist belong to the related financial-accelerator and empirical lineage, but the core theoretical credit is sharper for the pair. Bernanke-Gertler contributions are partly acknowledged through the 2022 prize.
assessment.maturity: Nearly three decades of use, including after the 2008 crisis, mean the contribution is well validated. Its influence on central-bank and academic modelling is widespread.
uncertainties: The 2022 prize on banks and financial crises may reduce the perceived urgency of this topic.
The right balance between the theory pair and the empirical financial-accelerator contributors is uncertain.
Direct empirical validation of the mechanism is mixed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Introduced firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory, changing how economists understand who exports, how trade liberalization reallocates resources and what the welfare gains are. It reoriented a field and links theory to firm-level microdata.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution. Helpman, with Melitz and Yeaple, extended it to the export-versus-FDI choice and developed the broader heterogeneous-firm research program. Redding is important for quantitative extensions but is less foundational for the core idea. Bernard, Eaton and Kortum are related but not on this ballot entry.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of development and extensive empirical confirmation. The 2008 prize recognized earlier new trade theory, and this is a distinct advance that is now standard.
uncertainties: Relationship to Krugman's 2008 prize and the prominence of Bernard, Eaton and Kortum in the same lineage.
The size of welfare gains from selection depends on model structure.
Helpman is also credited under another ballot entry, so the committee must choose where to place him.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework underpin modern central-bank practice, including the Taylor rule, forward-looking Phillips curves and optimal-policy analysis. The impact on policy and on academic macroeconomics is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Calvo's time-dependent pricing, Taylor's staggered contracts and policy rule, and Woodford's synthesis are central. Galí, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Gertler and Smets made major contributions to the estimated and policy-relevant models. The credit is widely distributed, so a three-person limit forces difficult exclusions.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely applied, with decades of data. The 2022 inflation episode has stress-tested the framework, with mixed verdicts.
uncertainties: Any three-person selection omits other major contributors, which creates an attribution problem.
Post-2021 inflation and the pass-through literature raise questions about the framework's empirical performance.
Ongoing debate about whether heterogeneous-agent models supersede the representative-agent version.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reshaped understanding of how technology and trade shocks alter labour demand, wages and regional employment. The task-based framework and the China-shock evidence changed public and academic debate on globalization and automation.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task approach and the trade-shock program. Hanson is the key co-originator on the trade side, and Dorn contributed substantively. Acemoglu's earlier prize partially overlaps with the task-based theory. Katz is credited for skill-biased change and the education-technology race.
assessment.maturity: The key papers date from roughly 2003 to 2016 and are widely replicated and debated. The long-run consequences are well documented.
uncertainties: The China-shock estimates depend on identification choices and design critiques.
Partial overlap with the 2024 prize on technology and institutions.
It is uncertain whether the committee prefers the trade or the technology emphasis.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opened a data-driven research program on long-run top-income and wealth distributions using tax records, which transformed the empirical study of inequality and its policy implications. The impact on public debate and measurement is very large.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez built the top-income series and the World Inequality Database lineage. Zucman is a younger leader on offshore wealth and distributional national accounts. Atkinson, who is deceased, was a pioneer, which complicates attribution.
assessment.maturity: The core income series date from the early 2000s and are widely replicated. The wealth-distribution and capital-return claims remain contested.
uncertainties: Methodological criticism of the wealth-share and capital-return conclusions.
Zucman's contributions are more recent.
Perceived policy advocacy might affect committee reception.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Built the intertemporal, microfounded open-economy macro framework, and its exchange-rate-disconnect and puzzle papers set the research agenda in international macro. The framework is the textbook basis for current-account, exchange-rate and international policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff share credit for the foundational text and the redux model, and each made separate major contributions. The pair is clearly identifiable. Rogoff is also credited under the crisis-history entry, so the committee must decide how to frame his contribution.
assessment.maturity: Foundational work from the 1990s, long established. The puzzles remain partly unresolved, which is both a strength for the agenda and a caution for the prize.
uncertainties: Several of the puzzles remain unsolved, so the question is whether a prize should reward the framework or its resolution.
Overlap with Mundell (1999) and the New Keynesian entries.
Pricing-currency and pass-through evidence is relevant, and I know that area from my own research, so my view may be influenced by familiarity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Provided the estimation toolkit for demand in differentiated-product markets (BLP) and for dynamic industry models, which now underpins merger review, antitrust and empirical industrial organization. The methods are used widely and shape competition policy.
assessment.attribution: Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes are the BLP originators, and Pakes also contributed to dynamic games and productivity estimation. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin are significant in the broader empirical-IO tradition. The BLP trio is the cleanest attribution.
assessment.maturity: BLP dates to 1995 and has been used for decades in academia and in agencies. It is a mature and validated tool.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as a methodological advance or a substantive discovery.
Identification and the sensitivity of structural estimates to functional-form assumptions.
I work in an adjacent field (IO), so this is a possible familiarity bias.
